title: The risks and benefits of long-term use of proton pump inhibitors: expert review and best practice advice from the American Gastroenterological Association
authors: Freedberg DE, Kim LS, Yang YX
funder: Not read: the publisher page refused access and the article is not in PubMed Central; PubMed indexes it as Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't.
result: Expert opinion and literature to July 2016, graded by a modified GRADE approach and reviewed by the AGA Clinical Practice Updates Committee. Patients with complicated GERD should take a PPI for healing, maintenance and long-term control; patients with uncomplicated GERD who respond should attempt to stop or reduce; patients with Barrett's oesophagus and symptoms should take a long-term PPI, asymptomatic patients should consider one; patients at high risk of NSAID ulcer bleeding should take a PPI; the dose should be periodically re-evaluated. Long-term users should not routinely use probiotics, raise intake of calcium, vitamin B12 or magnesium above the RDA, or be routinely screened or monitored for bone mineral density, serum creatinine, magnesium or vitamin B12; specific PPIs should not be chosen on the basis of potential risks.
